Description

G protein-coupled receptors reach ERK through β-arrestins as well as through G proteins. After angiotensin II activates its type 1A receptor (AGTR1), β-arrestin 2 binds the receptor, which is internalised, and on endosomal vesicles β-arrestin assembles RAF1, MEK1 and ERK2 into one complex. RAF1 bound to β-arrestin brings MEK1 and ERK2 together, and ERK2 is phosphorylated in the complex [1]. The protease-activated receptor 2 uses β-arrestin 1 in the same way. The internalised complex of receptor, β-arrestin, RAF1 and active ERK is needed for ERK activation, but the active ERK stays in the cytoplasm and neither enters the nucleus nor drives proliferation [2]. How stably a receptor holds β-arrestin sets how much active ERK is held in the cytoplasm and how much reaches the nucleus [3].

References

  1. Luttrell LM, Roudabush FL, Choy EW, Miller WE, Field ME, Pierce KL, et al. Activation and targeting of extracellular signal-regulated kinases by beta-arrestin scaffolds. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2001;98(5):2449-54. PMID: 11226259. doi: 10.1073/pnas.041604898.
  2. DeFea KA, Zalevsky J, Thoma MS, Déry O, Mullins RD, Bunnett NW. beta-arrestin-dependent endocytosis of proteinase-activated receptor 2 is required for intracellular targeting of activated ERK1/2. J Cell Biol. 2000;148(6):1267-81. PMID: 10725339. doi: 10.1083/jcb.148.6.1267.
  3. Tohgo A, Choy EW, Gesty-Palmer D, Pierce KL, Laporte S, Oakley RH, et al. The stability of the G protein-coupled receptor-beta-arrestin interaction determines the mechanism and functional consequence of ERK activation. J Biol Chem. 2003;278(8):6258-67. PMID: 12473660. doi: 10.1074/jbc.M212231200.
